newsitem.title: NORWAY: BP ends drilling in Norwegian Sea frontier well.
newsitem.headline: BP ends drilling in Norwegian Sea frontier well.

text.p: The Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) said on Wednesday that British Petroleum had completed deepwater exploration drilling in the frontier NYK High area in the Norwegian Sea.
The directorate, which said on June 12 that BP had found gas in the well reiterated that it was too early to give precise figures for the size of the find.
Preliminary estimates indicated between 40 to 60 million cubic metres of oil equivalent gas, or almost half the size of the North Sea Frigg field, it said.
No production test of the gas was made in the reservoir which lies about 3,000 metres below sea level in license 218.

"The probability of finding more gas in the area is extremely high, and there is also optimism that oil will be found," the OD said in a statement. "This is thus a good starting point for the exploraiton to continue."
It said more exploration would take place later this year in license 217, a neighbouring field to the west.

BP was awarded operatorship of licence 218 in Norway's 15th licensing round last year and holds a 25 percent stake. It is partnered by state oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS and Saga Petroleum ASA with 10 percent.
It was the first deepwater well to be spudded on the Norwegian continental shelf.
